title: A nonlinear immune-inflammation index fails to improve frozen FEV1 prediction beyond its component counts across NHANES cohorts
abstract: We tested whether nonlinear systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) structure improves prediction beyond flexible individual blood counts. Source-fitted spline ridge models used age, height, BMI, log platelet, log neutrophil and log lymphocyte counts, sex interactions, race/ethnicity and smoking. Adding log-SII spline terms was evaluated across separately recruited NHANES2007–2008 (n=3560) and2011–2012 (n=3553) cohorts. Target examination-weighted FEV1 MSE was 0.22604484 versus 0.22890882 L², delta +0.00286398 L² (joint source/target PSU-bootstrap95% interval [-0.00549140,+0.04872791]). The registered improvement criterion failed; influence diagnostics showed instability. This exploratory inconclusive negative result does not establish equivalence, causal effects, or absence of immune–lung association. Cohorts share a survey program and were previously used in published literature; validation in a separate study program remains unperformed.
